what_its_for: Clocortolone pivalate is a medium-strength steroid cream used to relieve redness, itching, swelling, and discomfort caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, psoriasis, rashes, and allergic skin reactions.
how_to_take: This medicine is for use on the skin only. Do not swallow it or get it in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer of cream and gently rub it in. Do not bandage or wrap the area tightly unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use more cream than directed, and do not apply it to larger areas of skin than instructed.
dosing: Apply a thin layer of cream to the affected skin area up to 3 times per day, or exactly as directed by your doctor. Use only the smallest amount needed to cover the affected area. Do not use this cream for longer than your doctor recommends.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular routine. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store the cream at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and freezing temperatures. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not apply to broken, infected, or open skin unless directed by your doctor. Avoid using this cream on your face, groin, or underarms unless specifically told to do so by your doctor. Do not use tight bandages, diapers, or plastic wrap over treated areas, as this can increase the amount of medication absorbed into your body and raise the risk of side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice any of the following: skin irritation, burning, stinging, or worsening of your condition after using the cream; signs of a skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, pus, or open sores; skin thinning, stretch marks, or easy bruising near the treated area; unusual hair growth or skin color changes; signs that the medication may be affecting your whole body, such as unusual weight gain, swelling, fatigue, or vision changes. These may be signs of too much steroid being absorbed into your body.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice improvement in redness, itching, and swelling within a few days of starting treatment. Full benefit is usually seen within 1 to 2 weeks. If your skin does not improve after 2 weeks of use, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Children: Use with extra caution in children, as their skin absorbs more medication than adult skin. Do not use this cream on a child's diaper area. Use the lowest amount needed for the shortest time possible, and only under a doctor's supervision. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this cream. Avoid applying it to large areas of the body or using it for long periods of time during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may have thinner, more fragile skin, so use the smallest effective amount and follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
